newsitem.title: USA: Cool, wet weather to continue in U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Cool, wet weather to continue in U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Cool, wet conditions were forecast for the U.S. Midwest next week, which may inhibit crop development but not damage them, meteorologists said.
The coldest weather should occur Friday night and Saturday morning in the Midwest, with temperatures in the mid 30s degrees Fahrenheit from eastern Illinois to Ohio.
"That's probably not going to do any (crop) damage," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Saturday will be warm, possibly in the 80s F, before cold returns late Sunday and remains through much of the week.

"It's going to be cold week next week," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather, who expected temperatures then to average 10 degrees below normal from the eastern Plains through the Midwest.
Scattered showers were forecast in parts of the Midwest, but Weather Services' Burgio said some spring planting should occur.
